general.reason: Appendix C states "The one Phase 2 harness file released here (output_noise_compaction.py) is the candidate that was ultimately kept," implying a candidate *was* accepted and applied, yet Section 6.3 says "Every candidate generated during the second optimization round performed worse than the existing agent, and its score *fell* to 59.1%." The paper never reconciles how applying a candidate that scored worse than A₁ (Transfer=68.2%) results in Final=59.1% rather than retaining A₁'s score, leaving the acceptance/rejection rule and the resulting regression internally inconsistent.

evidence.claim: The description of Meta Harness's Phase 2 'stall' is internally inconsistent regarding candidate acceptance/rejection based on evaluation feedback, making it unclear how a 9.1-point regression occurred.
evidence.excerpt: Section 6.3 says "Every candidate generated during the second optimization round performed worse than the existing agent, and its score fell to 59.1%," ... But Section 4.3 states Meta Harness "candidates are accepted or rejected based on evaluation feedback on the current task set." Under any acceptance rule that rejects candidates scoring worse than A₁, *all* candidates being worse would leave A₂ = A₁ and give Final = Transfer = 68.2%; instead Final = 59.1%, a 9.1-point regression. So either (a) a strictly-worse candidate was accepted anyway ... or (b) some candidates actually did *not* score worse ... rewrite the Phase 2 description so it is consistent with a candidate being kept even though its measured pass rate is lower than A₁'s.

judge_panel.reason: Appendix C states "The one Phase 2 harness file released here (output_noise_compaction.py) is the candidate that was ultimately kept," implying a candidate *was* accepted and applied, yet Section 6.3 says "Every candidate generated during the second optimization round performed worse than the existing agent, and its score *fell* to 59.1%." The paper never reconciles how applying a candidate that scored worse than A₁ (Transfer=68.2%) results in Final=59.1% rather than retaining A₁'s score, leaving the acceptance/rejection rule and the resulting regression internally inconsistent.

The paper does say Meta Harness 'candidates are accepted or rejected based on evaluation feedback on the current task set' (Sec. 4.3), yet also says 'Every candidate generated during Meta Harness’s second optimization round scored worse than its Phase-1-optimized agent' and that 'the candidate that was ultimately kept' is the released Phase 2 file (Appendix C). This makes the acceptance criterion unclear, but not strictly inconsistent, since the paper never states that only score-improving candidates can be kept.

The reviewer correctly identifies a logical contradiction in the paper. Section 4.3 states candidates are 'accepted or rejected based on evaluation feedback', yet Section 6.3 and Appendix C state 'Every candidate generated during Meta Harness’s second optimization round scored worse than its Phase-1-optimized agent, so its Phase 2 pass rate... fell' while also stating a candidate 'was ultimately kept', which contradicts the rejection mechanism.
